summary: Colostrum is the first milk produced after birth; bovine colostrum, used as a supplement, is rich in immunoglobulins (mainly IgG), lactoferrin, growth factors and other bioactive proteins. It is marketed to support immune function, gut health and athletic recovery, and has been studied for infectious diarrhea and gut-barrier conditions. It is NOT an FDA-approved drug; doses and uses below reflect supplement and reference information rather than an approved label.

moa: Bovine colostrum supplies preformed immunoglobulins (predominantly IgG) that can bind enteric pathogens and toxins within the gut lumen (passive local immunity), along with lactoferrin (antimicrobial, iron-binding), lysozyme, lactoperoxidase, cytokines, and growth factors such as IGF-1, EGF and TGF-beta that support intestinal epithelial growth and barrier integrity. These components are thought to modulate gut immunity, limit pathogen adhesion, and aid maintenance/repair of the gastrointestinal mucosa.

missed: If a dose is missed, simply take the next dose as usual - there is no need to double up. As a supplement, consistency over time matters more than any single dose.
overdose: Excessive intake is most likely to cause gastrointestinal upset (bloating, nausea, diarrhea) rather than serious toxicity. Reduce the dose or stop and manage symptoms supportively; seek care for any signs of allergic reaction.
